title: Amanta vs Purnimanta: why your festival date differs | Ask Tota
description: Half of India ends the lunar month at the new moon, half at the full moon. Same day, different month name. Here is why Janmashtami is Shravana in Mumbai and Bhadrapada in Delhi.
og_title: Why ur festival is on a different day from ur cousin's
og_description: Two lunar month conventions, one sky. Same festival, same day, two different month names, and occasionally a genuine one-day gap.
h1: why ur festival is named a different month in delhi
dek: half the country ends the lunar month at the new moon and half at the full moon. the sky is identical, the dates are almost always identical, and the month names are not. here is the whole thing, and the one case where the day really does differ.

faq.q: what is the difference between amanta and purnimanta?
faq.a: where the lunar month ends. an amanta month ends at the new moon, a purnimanta month ends at the full moon. same sky, two conventions, and they name the dark fortnight differently as a result.

faq.q: which parts of india use which?
faq.a: amanta is the norm across the south and west, including gujarat, maharashtra, karnataka, andhra, telangana, tamil nadu and kerala. purnimanta is the norm across the north, including up, bihar, madhya pradesh, rajasthan, punjab and haryana.

faq.q: does this change the actual festival date?
faq.a: almost never. the tithi is the same tithi and the day is the same day. what differs is which month name that day is filed under, so a purnimanta calendar calls it bhadrapada while an amanta one calls it shravana.

faq.q: why is janmashtami in a different month depending on who i ask?
faq.a: because it falls in the dark fortnight. krishna janmashtami is bhadrapada krishna ashtami in the north and shravana krishna ashtami in the west and south. one day, two names.

faq.q: is the bright fortnight the same in both systems?
faq.a: yes. shukla paksha carries the same month name in both conventions. only the dark fortnight, krishna paksha, gets shifted by one month name.
both. they are two regional conventions for labelling the same astronomy, and neither is a mistake. classical texts exist supporting each.

an extra lunar month inserted roughly every 32 or 33 months, so the lunar year does not drift away from the seasons. a lunar year is about eleven days short of a solar one and adhik maas is the correction.
the rare opposite, where a lunar month is dropped entirely. it can happen only in a narrow part of the year and only every century or so.

faq.q: can the actual day ever differ between two regions?
faq.a: yes, occasionally. it happens when a tithi changes close to sunrise and the two panchangs apply different rules about which tithi governs the day. that is a genuine one-day difference rather than a naming one.

faq.q: do solar calendars use this too?
faq.a: no. tamil, bengali, malayalam and punjabi solar calendars count months by the sun's entry into each sidereal sign, which is why their new year lands in april and does not move much.
no. a birth chart is computed from exact planetary positions, not from calendar labels. amanta and purnimanta are naming conventions and they never touch the maths.

faq.q: how do i know which convention my family uses?
faq.a: check what ur family calls the month that diwali falls in. purnimanta calls it kartik, amanta calls it ashwin. same festival, same night.
